prompt: Silhouette: Four-legged brown bear frame. Host frame: the brown bear sets the outline, body size and overall frame. A single creature that combines a european rhinoceros beetle and a brown bear. Head of the brown bear, fully visible and uncluttered, with clear, discernible eyes. Details: brown bear body and legs, with its own dense fur everywhere else, plain coat, no stripes or spots; from the european rhinoceros beetle, as parts and materials on the brown bear's own body: a single curved horn of hard, glossy chitin rising from the brow; a covering of hard, glossy chitin plates with fine seams in its own colors that replaces the brown bear's fur over the back and flanks: it grows in the skin as the brown bear's own covering there, not as pieces added on top; the fur stops at the covering's edge, and the belly and legs keep the brown bear's own fur; the covering is a carapace grown in the skin like an armadillo's, shaped like a beetle's two elytra: one domed dorsal shield from the shoulders to the hips, in two halves meeting at a midline seam, never scattered plates. The covering follows the body outline. Declared fiction: arthropod parts at large size, shown with thick supporting legs and visible breathing openings along the flanks. Bilaterally symmetrical, recognizable limbs, visible sense organs. Habitat cue (forest): dark back and light belly (mild countershading). Prosaic detail: natural lighting, feet in firm contact with the ground with a soft shadow, normal wear on hooves, claws and skin. One creature, full body, side three-quarter view, plain light background, natural history illustration. Material reference: use @Image1 only for the material of the chitin plates: their color, surface texture and seams. Do not copy its body, head, legs or shape; the creature is the brown bear described above.

spark_open.description: The creature is shown in right-facing side profile standing on a plain light background. It has the overall body, dense shaggy brown fur, head shape, and limbs of a bear, but its dorsal side from just behind the neck to above the hindquarters is covered by a large, highly glossy, dark reddish-brown beetle-like exoskeleton with strong specular highlights, longitudinal ridges, and small pits. A single large, glossy, dark brown to black, backward-curving horn with two small notches on its rear edge projects upward from the forehead. The animal stands quadrupedally with a thick furry neck, broad paws with pale claws, and only a very small tuft of fur visible at the rear beneath the shell.
